parsed.explanation: The combined regime's heaviest traveler-facing feature is the national document/entry regime now in force: X-markers halted, sex-binary passport rules upheld by the Supreme Court (Nov 2025), a visa cable instructing refusal where documents or evidence cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex and directing fraud-ground consideration with possible lifetime ineligibility, plus documented stranding and eight-plus foreign travel advisories. Layered on: a federal birth-sex facility ban in government buildings, a state school/college birth-certificate facility law (no enforcement mechanism, no arrests documented), narrowing state ID rules, and hostile official framing. Custody carries severe documented harm (conversion-therapy-style federal inmate policy; abuse in immigration custody). Mitigants are real but partial: courts enjoining several orders, a national hate-crime statute, employment protections, 33 municipal ordinances, no state criminalization of facility use.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented and in force: Feb 2025 stop of X/non-matching markers, Nov 2025 Supreme Court order letting passport sex-binary rules take effect; visa cable tells officers to refuse where discrepancy or 'reasonable doubt' on sex exists and to weigh fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; reports of passports blocked/confiscated and travelers stranded; allied governments issued advisories by Mar–Apr 2025.
entry_documents.protection: Suit by a national civil-liberties union remains pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ advises travelers; prior 1992 policy shows the regime is contested, not settled; no dossier evidence of routine document confiscation at this state's own borders.
entry_documents.interaction: A presentation/document discrepancy can escalate: entry refusal → fraud allegation → possible immigration detention, where documented federal custody abuses attach.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted (from 2026) a conversion-therapy-style inmate policy (forced haircuts, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution); reporting of trans prisoner numbers ceased in 2025. In immigration custody, trans men reported forced labor, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Elsewhere a trans woman was held 24 hours in a men's ward after a restroom arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: EO addressing LGBTQ rights in prisons was rescinded (hostile), but courts have enjoined other orders; no state-specific custody policy or monitoring data is sourced for this state.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or overstay findings can route a visitor into the immigration-detention system whose abuses are documented at federal level.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal EO bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities. State 'Protect All Students Act' (eff. 25 Feb 2025) requires all K-12 schools, colleges, public and private, to assign facilities by birth sex and students to use facilities matching birth certificates. Four states nationally criminalize such use in some circumstances; one documented arrest elsewhere involved a men's-ward hold.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The state statute has no enforcement mechanism and no arrest/citation is documented under it; single-occupancy restrooms exempt; 29 state/provinces plus units have no mapped ban; municipal ordinances exist in 33 cities/counties.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visiting student or accompanying parent in schools/colleges, or any visitor using federal buildings, meets the federal rule regardless of local tolerance; no documented remedy reaches facility refusal here.

care_services.exposure: State care/sports act (bans blockers/hormones/surgery for under-18s; sports exclusion) has been enjoined, allowed to take effect, and re-enjoined (18 Mar 2025) with a pending appeal — operative status unresolved. Jan 2024 perpetual-counseling rules were withdrawn. Nationally, orders call care 'mutilation' and proposed rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans patients.
care_services.protection: The re-injunction currently blocks the state's care ban for minors; adult emergency care, HRT continuity for adult visitors, and prescription handling are not documented as restricted here.
care_services.interaction: For an adult traveler this axis is largely open; for a traveling minor, litigation status decides exposure and could shift before travel.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National framing is hostile: EO language ('chemical and surgical mutilation'), a Dec 2025 reward memo invoking 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist viewpoints, and a May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritizing groups 'radically pro-transgender'; advocates compare the trajectory to early genocide stages. State level: ballot stripping of a trans candidate (Jan 2024), a Jan 2025 school staff out-LGBTQ-students-to-parents law, out-of-public-view signing over civil-rights objections.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward criterion does not list gender ideology itself and the strategy states counterterrorism powers won't target mere disagreement; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; employment discrimination barred nationally since 2020; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official rhetoric raises the probability and severity of every other axis (screening, police encounters) even where the memo's operative criteria are narrower.

minors_guardians.exposure: State facility law binds every public and private school and college by birth certificate; Jan 2025 law requires school staff to out LGBTQ students to parents and removes 'gender ideology' from K-3 curriculum; national EO directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; care/sports bans contested; national risk assessment (Jul 2026) rates this state second-highest of five tiers under 'Worst Policies In Effect'.
minors_guardians.protection: A traveling minor need not be enrolled locally; facility law has no enforcement mechanism; care ban currently re-enjoined; municipal conversion-therapy bans for minors in several cities; marriage and parental recognition unaffected.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's hospitalization or school visit could trigger birth-sex designation plus outing obligations; parent's own trans status meets the same border and facility regimes.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Travel guide (Apr 2026) advises checking recent violence reports and notes safety varies by state/province; national bias statistics show sexual-orientation bias at one-seventh to one-fifth of single-bias incidents; only 23 state/provinces cover gender identity in bias statutes and state has no gender-identity anti-discrimination statute.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute applies; a national appeals court covers the state and treats trans status as sex discrimination; no state presentation offense, no documented police extortion or identity-based sweeps against visitors here; a documented restroom arrest produced prosecution of the trans person (elsewhere), showing institutional risk rather than street violence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No documented pattern of street violence targeting trans visitors in this state; the state's own documented enforcement risk runs through institutions (ballot, schools, IDs), not街头 policing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport challenge unresolved after Supreme Court allowed the restriction; facility law has no enforcement mechanism and no complaints procedure is sourced; DMV Aug 2026 marker rules are an unsourced-to-rule-text announcement; counties still refuse birth-certificate corrections; risk-tier methodology unstated; no remedy documented for immigration-custody abuses or the federal inmate care policy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined multiple national orders and the state's care act; ACLU litigation continues; legal-aid FAQ operational; 33 municipal ordinances bar gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations; executive-order employment protection since 2018; national appeals court precedent since 2018.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy machinery works at the margins (employment, some facility rules) but has demonstrably failed on the border/document regime and does not reach custody or immigration detention.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-A there is an in-force tier-1 institutional exclusion (federal birth-sex facility ban plus the state school law) that a foreign passport cannot waive, and official threat-framing is stronger here (counterstrategy rhetoric, reward memo). But unlike 0.35-A, courts are actively enjoining national measures, the state facility law carries no enforcement mechanism or arrests, and municipal/national protections operate — so slightly above it.

0.45-D has a repeated, unremedied universal screening humiliation confined to transport. Here the universal exposure (entry document/doubt refusal, fraud/lifetime-ineligibility consideration, facility exclusion) is broader and its worst tail is worse (documented immigration-custody abuse, conversion-therapy-style inmate policy), while remedy record is comparable or weaker on documents — placing it below 0.45-D.

0.65-A assumes borders accept foreign passports without special scrutiny, service refusals get corrected, and courts convict attackers — a rule-of-law system where friction is remedied. Here the border regime is itself the exposure, foreign governments issue advisories, and custody harms are documented without remedy; acceptance of documents and functioning complaint routes are absent. Materially below 0.65.

0.55-E features repeated humiliating airport questioning with partial official correction and otherwise ordinary service. This dossier's border exposure is more consequential (refusal, fraud finding, stranding, foreign advisories) and adds custody and facility tiers 0.55-E lacks; its corrective institutions are also less effective on documents. Slightly below 0.55-E.

parsed.synthesis: The traveler meets one integrated system. At entry, the in-force document regime converts any appearance/document mismatch into refusal risk and possible fraud-based lifetime ineligibility, with no working remedy (the challenge is pending and the Supreme Court already let the rule take effect) — a universal-exposure border measure that also explains the foreign travel advisories. If that escalates, immigration detention attaches documented abuse. Inside, federal birth-sex facility rules plus the state's school/college birth-certificate law constrain gendered spaces, though the state statute is unenforced and unarrested and municipal ordinances soften private settings. Official rhetoric (counterterrorism strategy, EO language) raises the odds and severity of every encounter; courts, a hate-crime statute, employment protections and active civil society partially offset but have not displaced the border, custody or facility regimes — so no criminalization of presentation plus partial recourse still lands in Elevated Risk, not Reduced Risk.
